newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends up as meal gains ahead of USDA data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends up as meal gains ahead of USDA data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on gains in soymeal and on short covering before the release Thursday of USDA's world and U.S. supply/demand reports and weekly export sales report, traders said.
"It was short covering ahead of the s and d and before the sales. Tomorrow we'll have some numbers to trade off of," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co, of support in the pit Wednesday.

Talk circulated that USDA Thursday may trim 10 million to 20 million bushels from its estimate for 1996-97 U.S. soybean ending stocks. USDA's net export sales for soy for last week was expected to tally from 450,000 to 550,000 tonnes.
But most traders said the market was technically oversold for the near term and due for a bounce.
Commercial buying in soymeal was mentioned as a supportive influence with Continental Grain the chief purchaser of 1,200 lots, 600 of the total in the January, traders said.
But gains were limited by a drop in the Dow Industrial average and by near-ideal crop weather in South America soy regions.
Soybean futures closed 5-1/2 to 9-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with January up 6-1/2 at $6.91-1/2.
Key players in soybean futures included Farmers Commodities Corp with two million bushels purchased in the March and Lee B. Stern and Co bought two million January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 40,000 contracts, below the 46,359 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Cargill Investor Services sold 400 July $7.00 puts at 41-1/2 cents, LFG Futures bought 375 May $6.75 puts at 21-1/2 cents and Refco Inc sold 350 March $7.25 calls at 6-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents, traders said. Soybean options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, below the 14,933 traded Tuesday.
